Hi Liam / Anna —

Thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and next steps on the DPA/privacy points we discussed so your legal team has the right artifacts: 

1) Controller vs Processor: Redwood operates as a processor for inference-related requests. Customers remain the controller for customer data. We'll surface the exact language in the attached DPA (Redwood_DPA_v3.pdf).

2) Subprocessors: Attached is our current subprocessor list (subprocessor_list.csv). We notify customers 30 days in advance of material additions, and there is an opt-out workflow described in the DPA.

3) Breach notice / incident response: We commit to notify customers within 72 hours of confirming a breach that affects customer data; our Security Summary has the escalation contact info (Redwood_Security_Summary.pdf).

4) Data retention & logging: Customers can configure retention windows for request logs; defaults are 30 days for request-level logs, longer aggregated metrics retained per plan. We can support longer retention on Dedicated/Private deployments.

5) Data residency: Hosted data is stored in the region you select (US/eu/apac). For additional guarantees we can offer Private deployment or dedicated capacity options.

Next steps:
- I attached the current DPA and subprocessor list for your review.
- If you and legal have specific redlines, please send them back; I'll loop in our legal team.
- If it helps, I can schedule a short call between your legal and our counsel (Dev) — would tomorrow morning (PST) work?

Thanks — happy to tighten anything that needs clarity.

Hi all — happy to clarify. Short answers here and I attached a redline summary of the DPA with the relevant clauses highlighted.

1) Controller vs Processor: Redwood is a processor. We may process aggregated, anonymized telemetry to improve service quality, but that data is processed in an aggregated/non-identifiable form and the DPA includes explicit language that such telemetry is not customer personal data and is used for service improvement. We do not assume controller responsibilities for customer data under normal operation.

2) Subprocessors / locations: Our subprocessor list includes primary cloud providers with region mappings in the CSV; by default we supply the full list on request and we maintain a public subprocessor registry for transparency. If Sierra requires an EU-only subprocessor set, we can discuss options (Dedicated VPC or Private deployment preferred).

3) Breach notice: Our SLA is to notify customers within 72 hours of confirmation of a breach affecting customer data. The DPA language references "confirmation"; however, our incident response team will provide preliminary alerts earlier if there is a suspected issue and will provide an incident contact (sec-incident@redwood.com) for high-priority customers. We can assign a named incident lead for Dedicated/Enterprise contracts upon request.

4) Retention: Hosted default request-log retention is 30 days. We can extend to 1 year as an add-on for Hosted with a small storage surcharge; alternatively Dedicated customers can configure retention independently. I'll have Priyom follow up with estimated pricing impact for the Hosted add-on.

Attachments: Redline_DPA_summary.pdf (highlights), subprocessor_list.csv (annotated)

Regards,
